Artist Statement 1:
Do you feel unappreciated, lonely, or ignored sometimes? Do you regret things you have done? 

Those are undesirable emotions, but the Lord says he is near to the humble, the contrite in heart. I imagine pride is like a stench to God. Like when someone is talking to you and their hygeine is so bad that their breath and body smells. It's just hard to look past the fact that they are so oblivious to others that they don't care if they're making you miserable.

Maybe God likes those of us who at least care about becoming better people. We stay aware of if our soul is dirty. Sometimes we are aware of our brokenness in ways that we do not have the power to fix. But if we come to him with this on our hearts, at least we are open. 

And I think that is why those who are humble attract Him. It's because as long as we are ready to change, he's very happy to help make us clean, and stronger and beautiful again.

We Are In Control of Our First Thouths
excerpt:
Some mornings I wake up and my mind starts going in a way I don't want. For you it's probably about something different but for me it's usually about my romantic relationship stuff. It's crazy. Like an hour later I realize that's all I've been thinking about, stressful things I mean, and I'm coming to terms with the fact that that is not normal. 

And it's not healthy. It's been like this with every relationship I've been in and I've discovered this year it is very likely what psychologists call "Relationship OCD". It's a diagnosable illness. It'll be an uphill battle to manage it. It's in my nature, and probably for the rest of my life.

I've been trying to focus on prayer in the mornings. And through it I'm learning slow and little things. One of them is that I get to choose my thoughts.

Instead of getting out of the wrong side of the bed, I can choose to get out on the right side.  One way is to choose to pray as those first thoughts begin to barrage me. The easiest for me is to just start listing things I'm thankful for. At the top of my list is almost always... yep, my girlfriend. But then as I keep thanking God for things like my breath that feels so good, and that thing that happened yesterday, and my brothers and my family, I find myself praying FOR them. 

And an hour later I find I'm chest-deep in prayer. It takes a little push to get in that deep, and it seems a little unnatural during different seasons of life, but the habit of giving thanks is a good on-ramp. 

Raw Spoon, Jan 9, 2020.
